subject: Web Technology, Software Engineering & Emerging Technologies
exam_relevance: 4-6 questions expected in BPSC TRE CS exam

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web (WWW)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN, along with HTML, HTTP, and the first web browser.

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard markup language used to structure content on the web.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The (anchor) tag with the href attribute creates hyperlinks in HTML (e.g., text). links external resources.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to embed an image in a web page?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Images are embedded using the tag with src and alt attributes. None of , , or is the standard HTML tag.

questions.question: Which HTML tags define the main document structure of an HTML page?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An HTML document uses <html> as root, <head> for metadata/title, and <body> for visible content. All three are structural tags.

questions.question: Which HTML tags are used inside a <table> element to create rows and cells?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Inside <table>, <tr> defines rows, <td> defines standard data cells, and <th> defines header cells. All three are valid table tags.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to collect user input and submit it to a server?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The <form> tag creates an HTML form for user input (with <input>, <textarea>, <select>, etc.) and submits data via GET or POST.

questions.question: What is the main difference between HTTP and HTTPS?

options.A: HTTPS encrypts data using SSL/TLS whereas HTTP sends plaintext
options.B: HTTP supports multimedia while HTTPS only sends text
options.C: HTTP uses port 443 while HTTPS uses port 80
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over SSL/TLS (port 443), providing encrypted and authenticated communication, unlike plaintext HTTP (port 80).

questions.question: In the URL 'https://www.example.com:8080/page/index.html', what is 'https'?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In a URL, the first part before '://' is the protocol/scheme (https). 'www.example.com' is host/domain, '8080' is port, '/page/index.html' is path.

questions.question: Which HTML tag defines a paragraph of text?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
The

tag defines a paragraph in HTML. None of , , or is a standard HTML tag.

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily a client-side scripting language executed in the web browser?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: JavaScript runs directly inside the user's web browser (client-side) for DOM manipulation and interactivity. PHP and JSP execute on the server.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a server-side scripting language?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTML (markup), CSS (styling), and client-side JavaScript all run on the client browser. Server-side languages include PHP, ASP, JSP, Node.js.

questions.question: Which of the following are server-side web technologies?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: PHP, ASP, and JSP are all server-side scripting technologies that process requests on the web server and generate dynamic HTML responses.

questions.question: What does PHP stand for?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: PHP originally stood for Personal Home Page and now stands recursively for 'PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor'. It is a widely used server-side scripting language.

questions.question: Which runtime environment allows JavaScript to be executed on the server side?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that executes JavaScript code on the server side.

questions.question: In Java, which access specifier allows members to be accessed only by classes within the same package when no keyword is specified?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Java, omitting an access modifier gives package-private (default) access, making the member visible to all classes within the same package.

questions.question: Where does server-side script execution take place?

options.A: On the web server before sending the response to the client
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Server-side scripts execute on the web server, often interacting with databases, and send generated HTML/JSON output to the client's browser.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about client-side scripting (like browser JavaScript or VBScript)?

options.A: It reduces server load by validating forms in the browser
options.B: Its source code is visible to the end user
options.C: It directly accesses the server's database without an API
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Client-side scripts reduce server load (e.g., input validation) and their source code is visible in the browser, but they cannot directly access server DBs.

questions.question: Which SDLC model follows a strict linear sequential flow where each phase must be completed before the next begins?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Waterfall model is a linear, sequential SDLC model (Requirements → Design → Implementation → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance) with no easy backtracking.

questions.question: Which SDLC model explicitly emphasizes risk analysis in every iteration?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Barry Boehm's Spiral Model combines iterative development with systematic risk analysis in each loop (Planning, Risk Analysis, Engineering, Evaluation).

questions.question: Which SDLC model focuses on iterative delivery, customer collaboration, and responding to change over following a rigid plan?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Agile methodology delivers working software in short iterations (sprints) with continuous feedback and flexibility to accommodate changing requirements.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of building a software prototype in the Prototyping SDLC model?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a software prototype is to gather early user feedback and clarify unclear requirements before full-scale development.

questions.question: What does RAD stand for in Software Engineering?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: RAD stands for Rapid Application Development, an SDLC model emphasizing quick prototyping, reusable components, and rapid delivery (typically 60-90 days).

questions.question: Which is the first phase of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The first phase of SDLC is Requirement Gathering and Analysis (feasibility study & SRS), which precedes coding, testing, and deployment.

questions.question: What is an SRS document in Software Engineering?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SRS stands for Software Requirements Specification — a formal document describing functional and non-functional requirements of the software.

questions.question: In which situation is the Waterfall model MOST suitable?

options.A: When high risk requires frequent prototyping
options.B: When requirements are unclear and frequently changing
options.C: When requirements are well-understood, fixed, and stable
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Waterfall model works best when requirements are clearly defined, stable, and unlikely to change during development.

questions.question: Which SDLC phase consumes the largest share of effort and cost over the entire software lifespan?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Software Maintenance (bug fixes, enhancements, adaptation after deployment) typically consumes 60% or more of total lifecycle cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is an Agile software development framework?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Scrum, Extreme Programming (XP), and Kanban are all popular Agile frameworks emphasizing iterative delivery and collaboration.

questions.question: In the V-Model of software development, every development phase has a corresponding:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The V-Model (Verification and Validation model) pairs each development stage (Requirements, Design, Coding) with a matching testing stage.

questions.question: In software design, what is desirable for modular, maintainable software?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Good modular software design requires high cohesion within modules and low coupling (minimal inter-module dependency). All A, B, C are desirable.

questions.question: What is the main difference between Verification and Validation in software engineering?

options.A: Verification checks if built correctly; Validation checks if right product
options.B: Verification checks code; Validation checks only documentation
options.C: Verification is done by end users; Validation is done by developers
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Verification checks conformance to specifications ('building the product right'); Validation checks whether it meets user needs ('building the right product').

questions.question: Which testing technique examines internal code structure, logic, and execution paths?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: White-box (glass-box/structural) testing requires knowledge of internal code logic and paths. Black-box testing tests functionality without seeing code.

questions.question: Black-box testing focuses primarily on:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Black-box testing tests inputs against expected functional outputs from specifications without looking at internal code, DB schema, or CPU registers.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of testing levels from smallest scope to full system?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Testing progresses bottom-up: Unit testing (individual modules) → Integration testing (module interfaces) → System testing (entire system) → Acceptance testing.

questions.question: Which testing ensures that recent code changes have not broken existing functionality?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Regression testing re-runs existing test cases after bug fixes or modifications to verify that previously working features still work properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Black-Box testing technique?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Equivalence Partitioning (A) and Boundary Value Analysis (B) are both black-box techniques. Cyclomatic Complexity / path testing is white-box.

questions.question: Alpha testing is performed by:

options.A: End users at their own external sites
options.C: Internal staff/testers at the developer's site before release
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Alpha testing is done in-house at the developer's site; Beta testing is done by real end users in their own environment before final release.

questions.question: Unit testing is typically performed by:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Unit testing verifies individual functions, classes, or modules in isolation and is usually written and executed by software developers.

questions.question: Which of the following activities belong to Verification (static checking without executing code)?

options.C: Running stress tests on live servers
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Code walkthroughs (A) and formal inspections/reviews (B) are static verification techniques. Stress testing is dynamic validation/testing.

questions.question: Who introduced McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity metric used in white-box path testing?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Thomas J. McCabe introduced Cyclomatic Complexity V(G) = E - N + 2P in 1976. None of Barry Boehm, Dijkstra, or Gosling introduced it.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recognized subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, and Computer Vision (along with Robotics and Expert Systems) are all core subfields of AI.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a standard Turing Machine?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A standard Turing Machine consists of an infinite tape, read/write head, state register, and transition function. It does NOT have a separate output tape.

questions.question: In Machine Learning, training a model using labeled input-output pairs is called:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains on labeled data (classification and regression). Unsupervised learning finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., clustering).

questions.question: K-means clustering is an example of:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Clustering (such as K-means) groups unlabeled data points based on similarity, making it a classic Unsupervised Learning technique.

questions.question: What is the Turing Test designed to evaluate?

options.A: CPU clock speed of a computer
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, the Turing Test evaluates whether a machine can exhibit intelligent conversational behavior indistinguishable from a human.

questions.question: Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are computational models inspired by:

options.B: Biological neurons in the human brain
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Artificial Neural Networks are inspired by interconnected biological neurons in the brain, organized into input, hidden, and output layers.

questions.question: Which AI system emulates the decision-making ability of a human specialist using a knowledge base and inference engine?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An Expert System uses a Knowledge Base (facts & rules) and an Inference Engine to solve domain-specific problems like a human expert (e.g., MYCIN).

questions.question: Which search algorithm uses a heuristic function f(n) = g(n) + h(n) to find the optimal path?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A* search uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n), combining path cost so far g(n) and heuristic estimate h(n) to find an optimal path when h(n) is admissible.

questions.question: Amazon selling books and electronics directly to individual consumers is an example of which E-Commerce model?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: B2C (Business-to-Consumer) involves businesses selling products or services directly to individual end consumers (e.g., Amazon retail, Flipkart).

questions.question: OLX or eBay where individuals sell used goods to other individuals is an example of:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer) enables individuals to trade directly with other consumers via a platform (e.g., eBay, OLX).

questions.question: Alibaba connecting manufacturers and wholesalers with bulk business buyers is primarily an example of:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: B2B (Business-to-Business) involves transactions between businesses, such as manufacturers selling wholesale to retailers on Alibaba.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common E-Commerce business model?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: B2B, B2C, and C2B (e.g., freelancers/influencers offering services to businesses) are all valid E-Commerce models. Therefore, None of the above (E).

questions.question: A government portal allowing businesses to file taxes or bid on tenders online represents:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: B2G (Business-to-Government), also called B2A, covers online transactions between companies and government agencies (e.g., e-procurement, tax portals).

questions.question: What does EDI stand for in B2B E-Commerce?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: EDI stands for Electronic Data Interchange — computer-to-computer exchange of standard business documents between organizations.

questions.question: Which of the following are core elements of Multimedia?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Multimedia integrates five basic elements: Text, Images (graphics), Audio, Video, and Animation. All three options list valid elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is a well-known multimedia authoring tool?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Adobe Flash (originally Macromedia Flash, now Adobe Animate) and Macromedia/Adobe Director are classic multimedia authoring tools.

questions.question: Which file format uses lossy compression specifically designed for photographic images?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group) uses lossy compression for photographs. WAV is uncompressed audio; PNG/GIF use lossless image compression.

questions.question: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) files store:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: MIDI stores musical performance instructions (note pitch, duration, velocity, instrument) rather than sampled audio waveforms, keeping file sizes tiny.

questions.question: Which of the following are standard Cloud Computing service models?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Cloud computing has three primary service models: IaaS (e.g., AWS EC2), PaaS (e.g., Google App Engine), and SaaS (e.g., Gmail, Google Docs).

questions.question: Which emerging technology provides a decentralized, immutable distributed ledger of cryptographically linked blocks?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Blockchain is a decentralized, tamper-resistant distributed ledger storing transactions in cryptographically chained blocks. IoT connects physical devices.
